concrete_scene.heading: Worked adoption trace: one coil, four honest dispositions
concrete_scene.actor_or_system: A temporal-coil substrate candidate, an ordinary dense-or-learned fallback, a router consumer, and a negative control
concrete_scene.attempted_action: Move the same candidate from exploratory registration toward adoption by asking separately for structural, search-quality, and routing-quality authority under a named falsifier.
concrete_scene.observable_outcome: Structural evidence permits diagnostic use, unmeasured routing quality blocks adoption, and a failed wrong-period/nonperiodic control retires the measured-negative search route while preserving the fallback.
concrete_scene.failed_or_tested_boundary: The trace tests whether structural elegance or one proof can authorize an unmeasured consumer axis and whether a failed negative control can be ignored; both shortcuts are rejected.
concrete_scene.residual_owner: The substrate research owner retains the unmeasured quality axes, natural workload, implementation, cost, reproduction, and transfer obligations.
concrete_scene.evidence_boundary: All four dispositions are deterministic synthetic records rather than substrate A/B runs, so they establish adoption logic but no representation, search, routing, model-quality, or runtime advantage.

worked_trace.heading: Worked adoption trace: one coil, four honest dispositions
worked_trace.maximum_inference: The trace demonstrates axis-specific synthetic routing and retirement dispositions with eight rejecting controls; it establishes no substrate workload result, advantage, transfer, deployment, support transition, or SOTA claim.

counterexample_or_simpler_baseline: The simpler baseline treats a theorem or interesting architecture as general adoption evidence. The chapter keeps the ordinary substrate active and grants only the exact consumer axis that has passed its own baseline and control.
readable_claim: Elegant mathematics earns exactly the authority its evidence supports. A structural proof may justify a diagnostic lane while leaving search quality, downstream task quality, cost, and adoption entirely open.
normative_rule: Give every substrate a named ordinary baseline, workload, consumer, requested claim axis, negative control, falsifier, fallback, and retirement path. Only measured passing axes may change routing permission; an unmeasured axis, failed control, or theorem outside its statement blocks or retires adoption.

formal_binding.anchor: consumer-, use-, workload-, claim-axis-, implementation-, baseline-, resource-, and time-specific Substrate Adoption Lease

caveat_consolidation.local_caveat: The worked trace states once that its four dispositions are synthetic adoption records rather than executed substrate comparisons.
caveat_consolidation.consolidated_disposition: Implementation, workload, baseline, negative-control quality, resources, rights, reproduction, transfer, fallback, and theorem-boundary limits remain beside their specific candidate mechanisms.

bookkeeping_surface_disposition: The four-state trace remains in reader prose because the changing axis and permission are the argument; fourteen-source and nineteen-theorem inventories remain in reference surfaces.

editorial_diagnostics.mega_sentence_disposition: The short projections separate substrate curiosity, admission rule, and the complete formal lease.
editorial_diagnostics.hedge_disposition: One synthetic-trace boundary replaces diffuse caution while each candidate's workload, theorem, transfer, and performance limits remain explicit.
editorial_diagnostics.table_disposition: Source comparison and axis ledgers remain because they distinguish candidate roles and permissions rather than serve as project bookkeeping.

non_claims: The four dispositions do not execute a substrate A/B comparison.
The trace does not establish representation, search, routing, model-quality, or runtime benefit.
The editorial revision does not move chapter-core support or release state.
